selectedDefects.issueTitle: Typing 'F' in a text field attempts to full screen the page
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the application's webview preload claims the f key unconditionally, so the trigger crosses the real Electron guest boundary: a key delivered through the <webview> element API into a focused text field in the previewed page. That exercises the Electron adapter's action path and guest observation rather than a pure DOM assertion in the host renderer
selectedDefects.authority: platform: a printable key delivered to a focused text input must insert that character

manualReview.note: The affected preload registers a window keydown handler that calls preventDefault and requestFullscreen for f without checking the active element, so the character never reaches the input. The fix adds exactly that check. Under Xvfb the fullscreen request itself is rejected without dispatching fullscreenerror, so the campaign asserts the user-visible half of the defect -- the swallowed keystroke -- which is what the public issue reports and which is present on all three affected runs and absent on all three fixed runs. Typing a different printable key in the same focused input still reaches the page on the affected build, so the harness is proven able to deliver keys.

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Remember "Save image as" in the setting every time I open Upscayl
selectedDefects.whySuitable: an independent repository whose defect is a persisted-state contract rather than an input path, so the two applications exercise different parts of the Electron adapter: guest input delivery for one, renderer lifecycle and storage restore for the other
selectedDefects.authority: authored-contract: a setting the application persists must be restored on the next load

manualReview.note: The settings tab wrote localStorage saveImageAs as a bare string on top of the jotai atomWithStorage entry for the same key. atomWithStorage stores JSON, so the bare value failed to parse on the next load and the setting reverted to the png default. The campaign observes exactly that: after choosing jpg the affected build stores jpg and shows png again after a reload, while the fixed build stores "jpg" and restores it. A second setting persisted through the same mechanism survives the same reload on the affected build, so the reload itself is not what loses state.

corpus.note: The adversarial subjects are the two legal explanations for the same observable as the webview defect: a guest page that claims the key itself, and an input that accepts no characters at all. The first is settled by the page's own recorded suppression, which is a property of this corpus rather than a general capability against arbitrary pages; the second is settled by delivering the control key, which needs no instrumentation.
